title: Min
capsule: Min (閩) was one of the Ten Kingdoms of the Five Dynasties period, occupying Fujian province in southeastern China from 909 to 945. It was founded by Wang Shenzhi, who had governed Fujian since 893 as a subordinate of the Tang and declared himself king after its fall; his cautious administration, low taxes, and promotion of maritime trade brought relative prosperity to the mountainous province. After Wang Shenzhi's death in 925, his sons engaged in fratricide and succession wars — Wang Yanjun proclaimed himself emperor in 933 — that shattered central authority. The state of Southern Tang invaded in 945, but Yin (a breakaway Min statelet under Wang Yanzheng) survived until 963, when it too was absorbed by the Wuyue kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Min's territory is well-defined by Fujian's natural mountain boundaries; Chinese dynastic histories provide detailed political narrative, making the kingdom's extent among the better-attested of the Ten Kingdoms.
